title: Odile and the Songbook
premise: Mara Quintana, a wedding planner whose own engagement ended in betrayal, is assigned an anonymous pen-pal exchange through her sister's bookshop—only to discover her letters are going to Theo Vance, the estate lawyer dismantling the inheritance of the songbook her late grandmother left her. Their correspondence turns from hostility to intimacy before either learns the other's identity, and when Theo reveals the songbook legally belongs to a predatory music publisher, Mara must choose between the justice she can win in court and the truth she can only win by exposing her family's old secret. In the end, they forfeit the lawsuit, publish the songs under her grandmother's name, and Mara risks the whole heart—choosing Theo at the very wedding she planned for strangers.
about_author: Sable Dravenmoor is the pen name of a former wedding pianist who spent a decade watching love arrive on schedule and leave off-script. She writes romances about people who keep their hearts in escrow until someone finally calls in the debt.

chapters.title: The Anonymous Correspondents
chapters.summary: Mara's POV. Grieving her broken engagement and planning weddings she no longer believes in, Mara grudgingly joins her sister's bookshop pen-pal program, writing one guarded letter about her grandmother's songbook. The reply arrives sharp, skeptical, and strangely alive. Emotional beat: reluctant hope—a woman who keeps love in the past tense feeling, against her will, a pull toward the present.

chapters.title: Letters Against the Law
chapters.summary: Alternating POV between Mara and Theo Vance, who doesn't know his anonymous correspondent is the Quintana heir he's legally bound to oppose. Their letters deepen into confession while, in person, they clash over the publisher's claim to the songbook. Emotional beat: dramatic irony tightening—the reader knows what they don't, and every barb they trade in daylight lands tenderly on paper.

chapters.title: The Name Behind the Ink
chapters.summary: Theo's POV. Discovering Mara's identity mid-correspondence, Theo must decide whether loyalty to his firm or truth to her matters more; Mara, learning it first, feels the old betrayal pattern repeating and burns his letters. He chooses her over the case, confessing everything at the bookshop. Emotional beat: climax of trust—love surviving the exact wound that taught her to hide.

chapters.title: Everything I Meant to Send
chapters.summary: Mara's POV. They withdraw the suit and publish the songbook under her grandmother's name, justice achieved outside the law. At the seaside wedding she's coordinating for two clients, Theo appears with the unsent letters and her grandmother's final song. Emotional beat: resolution—Mara stops lending pieces of her heart and gives the whole thing, dancing to a song that was always meant to be sung aloud.
